subject: Re: Follow-up: Rate limits & overage pricing — burst usage and quota increases
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Rate limits & overage pricing — burst usage and quota increases

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned on pricing and operational expectations: 

1) High-level numbers you shared
- Expected steady-state: ~100M tokens/month
- Peak/burst days: up to ~300M tokens (short spikes tied to campaign launches)
- Target budget: ~$12 to $15 per 1M tokens (this is your procurement target range)

2) What matters most to you
- Predictable unit economics (target $/1M tokens)
- Capacity for short bursts without impacting latency or dropping requests
- Clear overage terms and a straightforward process for increasing quota during launches

3) Two pragmatic options for Acme (summary)
A) Hosted, usage-based (fastest onboarding)
   - Standard rate: $20 / 1M tokens
   - Monthly soft quota: configurable (e.g., 150M tokens)
   - Burst policy: auto-burst up to 2x soft quota for 24 hours; overage beyond that billed at $30 / 1M tokens unless we agree a temporary quota raise
   - Quota increase lead time: 72 hours for scheduled increases; emergency raise available via priority support (subject to approval)

B) Reserved (Dedicated) commitment
   - Example commitment: 500M tokens/month at $12 / 1M tokens (meets your target)
   - Includes headroom for bursts; negotiated SLA and predictable unit cost
   - Can pair with a modest overage rate (e.g., $15-$20 / 1M tokens) for true overages

4) Suggested next steps
- Can you confirm whether the 100M steady / 300M peak are accurate ranges for the first 6 months? If yes, I can run a cost comparison for: (i) Hosted usage with a 150M soft quota + burst protections vs (ii) Dedicated 500M commit priced to your $12/1M target.
- If procurement wants a target line-item for $/1M tokens, we can craft a two-line quote showing committed vs overage pricing for the RFP.

Attachments: I attached the usage estimate template (Acme-MA-usage-estimate.xlsx) and our public rate card (Redwood-ratecard-2026Q2.pdf) for reference.

I'll leave Rafael and Marissa on this thread for procurement/CS ops follow-up. Happy to jump on a short call with procurement to walk the numbers.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.io>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.io>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Rate limits & overage pricing — burst usage and quota increases

Thanks, Camila — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 100M steady number is conservative for Q3; we may ramp to ~150M steady by Q4.
- The 300M peak is a realistic upper bound for 1–2 day campaign launches, but those are rare (2–3 times/year).
- Procurement confirms target $/1M is $12 if we can get a 12-month commit. If not, $15 is the ceiling.

Questions:
1) For the hosted option, can you confirm SLA behavior during bursts? We need to avoid dropped requests — at worst we want queued requests or graceful 429s with retry guidance.
2) For emergency quota increases (same-day), what is the approval flow and what are typical lead times?
3) If we commit to a 12-month 500M/month reserved plan, is the $12/1M inclusive of all tokens (prompt+completion) or are there exclusions?

Procurement asked that we get a sample contract clause on overage billing (how we measure tokens, invoice cadence, and any minimum billing increments). Can you and Marissa draft that?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 20-min call if that speeds things up.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
alex.j@acme.io

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Rate limits & overage pricing — burst usage and quota increases

Alex — great questions. Quick answers below and I drafted the verbiage procurement requested (see inline).

1) SLA behavior during bursts- Hosted: We prioritize requests based on route and customer tier. For bursts within the auto-burst window (up to 2x soft quota for a 24-hour period) we maintain latency SLAs; requests are not dropped. If capacity is constrained beyond the auto-burst window, the system will return 429s with a Retry-After header and we provide exponential-backoff guidance in the SDK. For Dedicated customers the likelihood of enforced 429s is negligible as long as usage stays within committed capacity + agreed headroom.

2) Emergency quota increases- Flow: submit a request to priority-support@redwood.ai (cc: your CSM). Typical response within 2 hours; gated approval based on available capacity and credit checks. For sustained increases we require a 72-hour lead time to provision additional autoscaling. For campaign day immediate bumps we can often enable a temporary soft increase (subject to T&Cs) for up to 48 hours.

3) What the committed price covers- Committed 500M/month at $12/1M would be inclusive of prompt + completion tokens measured by our standard tokenizer (we provide the tokenization method in the contract appendix). Model-specific multipliers are not applied — token accounting is consistent across supported models in the agreement.

Draft overage clause (procurement-friendly)
- Measurement: Tokens are measured using Redwood's standard tokenizer for the deployed model (documented in appendix A).
- Invoice cadence: Monthly in arrears; overage charges are listed as a separate line item.
- Minimum billing increment: 1,000 tokens; overages below this are aggregated to the nearest 1,000 tokens for billing.
- Overage rate: For customers on a committed Reserved plan, overage during normal operations will be billed at $15 / 1M tokens. Ad-hoc emergency bursts enabled via priority support may be billed at a short-term overage rate of $30 / 1M tokens if capacity is provisioned on a third-party rental basis.

Next steps I can take this week
- Rafael and I will prepare a two-line commercial showing: (A) 500M/mo Reserved @ $12/1M + $15/1M overage, and (B) Hosted plan with 150M soft quota @ $20/1M with auto-burst to 300M/day and $30/1M overage.
- Marissa will draft the contract clause with the tokenization appendix and a sample SLA excerpt.

If that sounds good I'll schedule a 20-min call with procurement for Thursday to run through the two-line comparison and the procurement language.

Best,
Camila
